angle: Borrow a calibrated process model instead of learning physics: SPARROW / SWAT / Iowa NRS outputs as features
verdict: PURSUE, BUT NOT AS FRAMED. The angle splits cleanly into two halves with radically different evidence, and only one is worth acting on. (1) The DATA-ACQUISITION half is verified, cheap, and deployment-compatible, and it is the recommendation: the USGS Midwest 2012 SPARROW data release (DOI 10.5066/P93QMXC9) is a free, unauthenticated, per-NHDPlusV2-COMID table that this project can join directly to its already-stored basin COMIDs with no modeling, no API, and no rate limit. Its single most valuable content is not the model OUTPUT but the model INPUT file, which contains a per-catchment tile-drainage percentage (tiles13_perc2) — closing, verified, the project's stated gap that tile drainage is 'the dominant hydrologic control in Iowa' with 'NO data source identified yet' — plus complete, multi-state-covering 2012 fertilizer/manure/atmospheric/fixation nitrogen source terms that repair the gTREND-ends-in-2017 (68% NaN) problem and the documented Iowa-boundary inner-join undercount. All of these are STATIC per-basin scalars, which is exactly the shape of the project's actual deficit (between_r2 0.21 vs within_r2 0.42) and is the one feature class that has historically worked here while every temporal feature failed. (2) The PROCESS-GUIDED-ML half is NOT supported by any verified evidence in this corpus. Every claim about Read et al., Jia et al., and Willard et al. — pretraining on process-model output, physics-informed losses, meta-transfer to unmonitored sites — arrived at tier 3 and was never adversarially verified, so none of its numbers may warrant a recommendation here. Even taken as leads, that literature points away from the ambitious version: the pretraining recipe is an LSTM weight warm-start that does not port to XGBoost, and its reported benefit is concentrated in TEMPORAL label scarcity at monitored sites, which is the opposite of this project's regime (160k labeled rows, 19 independent sites). THREE EXPECTATION-SETTERS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THE RECOMMENDATION. First, SPARROW's headline numbers are a trap: R2 0.950 / Yield R2 0.913 are IN-SAMPLE calibration fit on the same 1,334 sites that estimated the coefficients, with no cross-validation, no spatial holdout, and no independent test set anywhere in the 74-page report; they are also on a different target (long-term mean-annual TN LOAD, kg/yr, base year 2012) than daily-max nitrate concentration exceedance. They must never be quoted next to LOFO 0.820. Second, the project's own prior about tile drainage is contradicted by the best available fit: SPARROW's ln(tile %) coefficient is +0.101, statistically strong (p<0.0001, t=4.5) but a modest elasticity — doubling tile percentage raises modeled N delivery only ~7.3% — versus ln(runoff) at 0.673. Tile drains are the WEAKEST significant land-to-water term in SPARROW's own TN fit. Expect a real but small between-site contribution, not a fix for between_r2 0.21. Third, the circularity worry that motivated this angle turns out to be largely defused: the public release ships UNCONDITIONED simulated loads, computed identically at monitored and unmonitored reaches from catchment attributes and ~14-15 globally shared coefficients, so any one Iowa site's leverage is on the order of 1/1,334 rather than site-level memorization. The audit is still cheap and worth running once, but it is not a blocker. NET: this is a low-cost, low-risk, correctly-targeted acquisition play with an honest expected gain that is small and, at n=19 folds, may not be statistically distinguishable from fold noise. Budget a few days, add 3-5 hand-picked static columns, pre-register that a <0.03 PR-AUC LOFO gain is a null, and do NOT budget for a PGDL rebuild.

findings.claim: A per-NHDPlusV2-catchment TILE DRAINAGE percentage is already published and free, closing the project's stated 'no data source identified' gap. The Midwest SPARROW TN model uses 'Ln (tile drains, percentage of catchment)' as a land-to-water delivery term with coefficient +0.101 (90% CI 0.064-0.139, SE 0.023, p<0.0001, t=4.5, VIF 2.3), and the underlying per-catchment values ship as columns tiles13_perc2 / ltiles13_perc2 inside the freely downloadable mw_sparrow_model_input.txt, keyed by ComID. Source layer is Nakagaki & Wieczorek (2016), tile-drainage extent for 12 Midwest states, circa-2012 vintage (the '13' in the column name is a naming artifact, NOT the data year), extrapolated to NHDPlusV2 catchments by Wieczorek et al. (2019), with ND/SD gap-filled from tile-permit polygons. IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE PROJECT'S PRIOR: the effect is statistically strong but a MODEST elasticity. In a ln-ln delivery term, 0.101 means doubling tile percentage raises modeled TN delivery by only ~7.3% (2^0.101), and a 10x increase by ~26%. In the same table ln(runoff) carries 0.673, ln(soil clay) 0.292, ln(no-till) 0.124. Tile drains are the WEAKEST significant land-to-water delivery term in SPARROW's own TN fit — runoff dominates by roughly 7x in log-space elasticity. The project's belief that tile drainage is 'the dominant hydrologic control in Iowa' is not supported by this model. Note also that the identical variable enters the companion TP model with a NEGATIVE coefficient (-0.091, 90% CI -0.156 to -0.026, p=0.0221, t=-2.3), so the term is doing pathway-partitioning work, not acting as a universal 'more tile = more nutrient' flag; only the TN sign is relevant here.
findings.effectSize: ln(tile %) TN coefficient +0.101, 90% CI [0.064, 0.139], SE 0.023, p<0.0001, t=4.5, VIF 2.3. Elasticity: +7.3% delivery per doubling of tile %. Compare ln(runoff) 0.673. TP counterpart -0.091 (p=0.0221). NHDPlusV2 catchments mean 2.7 km2.

findings.feasibilityAtN19: HIGH — and this is the one place the n=19 flag genuinely does not bite. The evidence base is 1,334 basins, 70x this project's 19 independent families, which would normally disqualify a method. But what is being imported is a DATASET COLUMN, not a fitted method: nobody is transferring the 0.101 coefficient. One static per-basin covariate is the cheapest possible test of the between-site hypothesis and costs ~1 degree of freedom against 19 units. CAUTION IN THE OTHER DIRECTION: tile drainage in Iowa is strongly spatially structured (Des Moines Lobe vs driftless/loess), so it will correlate with lat/lon — already the model's #2 and #3 permutation-importance features — and marginal gain over existing geography may be near zero even though the physics is real. Add ONE scalar basin-mean tile fraction; do NOT add linear and log forms across all three distance buckets, which is 6 spatially-smooth columns against 19 units.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES, fully. Static per-catchment attribute keyed by COMID, defined everywhere in the 12-state footprint. Pipeline: map pin -> NLDI upstream COMID list -> join tiles13_perc2 -> area-weight by IncAreaKm2. No local nitrate history, no discharge gauge, no monitored upstream neighbor required. The project already stores NHDPlus comid per basin, so this is a table join, not new geoprocessing.

findings.claim: SPARROW Midwest 2012 model output is downloadable per NHDPlusV2 reach with no authentication, and supplies exactly the shape of feature this project's diagnostics call for: a static per-basin ABSOLUTE-LEVEL term. The TN output file (mw_sparrow_model_output_TN.txt, 493 MB, plain CSV, 40 columns, ~1.38M rows, one per COMID) carries accumulated TN load (al_tn) and INCREMENTAL TN load (il_tn), each decomposed into seven source shares (wwtp, fert, man, atm, urb, nfix, can) with per-reach standard errors (alse_*/ilse_*), plus DEL_FRAC (delivery fraction), SE_DEL_FRAC, res_decay and se_res_decay. Incremental TN yield is derivable as il_tn/IncAreaKm2 and a flow-weighted mean concentration from al_tn and wbm_meanq. Units are NOT documented in the release — the FGDC metadata XML is listed at size 0 and its download URL returns 404, and ?format=xml returns 415 — but were established empirically as kg/yr for all al_*/il_* load columns and cfs for wbm_meanq, cross-checked by the resulting concentrations landing in a physically plausible 0.4-7.6 mg/L range Midwest-wide. Because SPARROW output is a mean-annual steady-state quantity it can ONLY move the between-site term, which is precisely where this project's diagnostics locate essentially all remaining headroom (between_r2 0.21, between_rate_r2 0.24) and precisely where the seven failed temporal ablations say the deficit is NOT.

findings.feasibilityAtN19: MODERATE. Attaching the data is trivial; DETECTING a gain is not. Under LOFO these collapse to at most 19 distinct effective values, so adding many correlated static SPARROW columns is a ~20-parameter regression on 19 independent units. Add a small pre-selected set — incremental TN yield, one or two dominant source shares, DEL_FRAC — not all 40 columns, with the count fixed a priori rather than chosen on LOFO score. Expect wide per-fold error bars; a gain below roughly 0.03 PR-AUC will not be separable from fold noise. Report per-fold spread, not just the mean, and judge against between_rate_r2 0.24 / between_r2 0.21 rather than overall AUC.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES. Values exist at every COMID in the Midwest network, computed identically at monitored and unmonitored reaches. Requires no target-site observations and no gauged upstream neighbor.

findings.claim: SPARROW's published fit statistics must NOT be used as a benchmark or as evidence of ungauged skill, and this is the single most important guard on this whole angle. The 2012 Midwest SPARROW TN model reports R2 = 0.950 (log accumulated load), Yield R2 = 0.913, conditioned RMSE 0.487 natural-log units (51.8% real space) and unconditioned RMSE 0.555 log units (60.0% real space). These are pure IN-SAMPLE calibration statistics: the same 1,334 sites' measured loads estimated the coefficients, and an exhaustive read of the 74-page report (88 PDF pages, 5 appendixes) confirms it contains NO cross-validation, NO leave-one-basin-out, and NO independent test set anywhere. The model is a 17-variable regression with 14-15 freely estimated coefficients (3 terms are fixed rather than fitted: Canada load = 1.0, public-supply surface-water withdrawal = 1.0, groundwater-irrigation pumping loss = 1.221, all showing '--' for SE, p and t). FOUR SEPARATE REASONS THESE NUMBERS ARE NON-COMPARABLE TO LOFO 0.820 / R2 0.328: (a) no spatial holdout of any kind; (b) different response variable — long-term mean-annual TN LOAD in kg/yr for a 2012 base year, versus daily-max nitrate CONCENTRATION exceedance of 10 mg/L; (c) different time scale — SPARROW is steady-state with no time dimension at all, so it says nothing about daily exceedance timing; (d) different variance denominator — Yield R2 0.913 is cross-sectional across a continental domain (Dakotas to Ohio) where yields span orders of magnitude, while between_r2 0.21 is across 19 Iowa corn-belt families with a severely restricted between-site range. Further, the 'conditioned' RMSE (0.487) resets predicted accumulated loads to MEASURED loads at upstream calibration sites — a gauged-upstream-neighbor protocol that DOES NOT WORK for the arbitrary-map-pin target. Only the unconditioned 0.555 applies to a reach with no upstream measurements, and even that remains an in-sample number: it removes the upstream conditioning but not calibration-set membership, so 0.555 ln-units is a LOWER BOUND on true ungauged error, not an estimate of it. Two internal signals confirm the honest expectation is worse: residuals are spatially autocorrelated (Moran's I 0.199, p=0.0005) with systematic regional over/underprediction — i.e. the between-site level bias that is this project's core problem is present in SPARROW too, even in-sample — and unconditioned RMSE degrades from 0.39 to 0.65 log units for TN loads below 14 ln-units, meaning accuracy is worst precisely at the small headwater basins an arbitrary map pin most often lands on.
findings.effectSize: R2 0.950 (accumulated load, log units); Yield R2 0.913; conditioned RMSE 0.487 ln-units = 51.8% real space; unconditioned RMSE 0.555 ln-units = 60.0% real space; mean exponentiated weighted error 1.129. Typical multiplicative error factor 1.6x (as a 60% real-space CV) to 1.74x (as exp(0.555), a one-sigma multiplicative spread) — state as a range, the two conventions differ. Small-load degradation: unconditioned RMSE 0.65 (ln load < 14) vs 0.39 (> 14). Residual Moran's I 0.199, p=0.0005. Weaker constituents show a much larger load-vs-yield gap (SS R2 0.837 vs Yield R2 0.651; TP R2 0.875 vs Yield R2 0.741).

findings.claim: The CIRCULARITY concern that motivates this angle is REAL BUT BOUNDED, and the initial framing of it was too alarmed. Verified provenance facts: the SPARROW TN calibration loads were assembled from water-quality data contributed by 71 Federal, State, regional, local, Tribal, university and private agencies, and appendix 3 (Table 3.1) of SIR 2019-5114 explicitly lists FIVE Iowa providers — 'IA DNR — Iowa Department of Natural Resources', 'IA DMWW — Des Moines Water Works, Iowa', 'IA GSWSP — Iowa Geological Survey Watershed Snapshots', 'IA ISUCOE — Des Moines River Water Quality Network', and 'IA VWMP — Iowa Volunteer Water Monitoring Program'. Site-inclusion criteria: >=3 years of record, >=24 samples, >=3 samples in each of four 3-month seasons, period of record within 3 years of the 2012 base year, and a paired streamgage with >=10 years of gap-free daily flow including 2012, within 40 km, with watershed-area ratio 0.75-1.33 (relaxed for WQ basins under 260 km2). Data compilation window 1999-10-01 to 2014-09-30, so the effective calibration period of record is roughly 2009-2014. HOWEVER, THE LEAKAGE MECHANISM IS MUCH WEAKER THAN 'SPARROW ENCODES THAT SITE'S OWN LEVEL'. Load-substitution ('conditioning') is applied during calibration and to the calibration RMSE, NOT to the distributed reach predictions; the public data release ships ONLY unconditioned simulated loads, and the output file contains no station ID, no measured load and no residual. A reach's published SPARROW value is therefore a deterministic function of that catchment's attributes and ~14-15 globally shared coefficients, computed identically at monitored and unmonitored reaches. A given Iowa site's own observations enter only as roughly 1/1,334 of a Midwest-wide coefficient fit, further downweighted by the report's nested-share weighting scheme. Add that the target quantities differ — a fully contaminated reach would leak a slow basin-average annual LOAD level, never the daily 10 mg/L label. NET RECOMMENDATION: keep the audit, drop the alarm. Before publishing any LOFO gain from a SPARROW-derived feature, join the ~85 sites against the calibration-site table by COMID plus a distance tolerance (COMID-exact matching alone will under-detect, since the report permits a WQ site up to 40 km from its paired gauge) and report how many FAMILIES, not sites, contain a TN calibration site; at only 19 folds even 3-4 contaminated families warrants a caveat, which is why the check is cheap insurance despite the diffuse mechanism. Report the gain with and without those families and treat the gap as the optimism bias. The inference that IWQIS sensor sites are cleaner is logically sound — a post-2015-only record cannot satisfy 'period of record within 3 years of 2012' plus 24 samples — but IA DNR is a listed provider and many IWQIS sensors sit at USGS gauges, so this must be checked per site rather than assumed by network. FINALLY, NOTE THE LEAK IS EVALUATION-SIDE ONLY: SPARROW output is defined at every COMID, so even under full contamination the feature remains usable in the shipped product; the consequence would be that a LOFO score overstates what a genuinely unmonitored pin receives, not that the feature fails at deployment.

findings.claim: The SPARROW model INPUT file is a ready-made, complete, multi-state static nitrogen-driver table that repairs TWO documented data defects in this project simultaneously — but it must be whitelisted, not ingested wholesale. mw_sparrow_model_input.txt is an 89-column per-catchment attribute table keyed by ComID (mixed case; note huc12 is lowercase and blank for some rows, so a literal 'HUC12' lookup will KeyError). Verified safe driver columns include: ManN2012 (manure N), fert_sw_N_kg (farm fertilizer N), cmaq_TN_12_kg (CMAQ atmospheric N deposition), nfix_km2 (biological fixation), CAT_PFARM1 (CRP relative to farmland), lCAT_notill, tiles13_perc2/ltiles13_perc2, CAT_STCLAY/lcat_STCLAY (soil clay), lcat_KFCTUP (erodibility), ldrainden (drainage density), wbm_incq_mm (incremental runoff), lPPT_INT, CAT_ELEV, TAV_AVE, DTtav2012, IncAreaKm2, CumAreaKm2, HUC8, STATE. DEFECT 1 REPAIRED: the gTREND nitrogen-surplus product ends in 2017 and is NaN for 68% of training rows; ManN2012 + fert_sw_N_kg + cmaq_TN_12_kg + nfix_km2 are complete across the region. DEFECT 2 REPAIRED: the 16.5%-of-cells inner-join undercount that silently deflates crop area and N surplus for basins extending outside Iowa is avoided entirely, because SPARROW inputs are populated across the full multi-state model domain including MN, SD, NE, MO, WI and IL. CRITICAL QUALIFICATION ON DEFECT 1 — THIS IS A SUPPLEMENT, NOT A SUBSTITUTE. These are single-year 2012 static snapshots with zero temporal dimension. They replace a 68%-NaN time series with a complete constant; they cannot recover time-varying N-input variation, they remove it. The project already has a directly analogous negative result — broadcasting 2017 N-surplus forward in time scored lofo_r2 -0.166 — so these must be ADDED as static between-site covariates, one value per basin never varying by day, and must NEVER be substituted into the existing time-varying slot, or that exact failure is likely to reproduce. The distinction that may rescue them is that a genuinely time-invariant covariate introduces no spurious temporal step and loads purely on the between-site term, but that is an untested hypothesis, not an established result.

findings.feasibilityAtN19: LOW-TO-MODERATE, and this is where the n=19 constraint bites HARDEST in the whole angle. Once aggregated to basin means these collapse to ~19 effective independent units; adding ~20 static columns against 19 units is a p>n setup in which LOFO cannot reliably distinguish real transfer from noise. Amplifying this, the report's own caveat states that 'much of the source data and landscape data used to describe variability in land-to-water delivery were derived from county-wide averages or totals' apportioned to catchments by fine-scale land use — so realized between-site resolution is COUNTY-scale, which within a single Iowa basin family is close to constant, making these high-variance additions prone to memorizing family identity. RECOMMENDATION: 3-5 hand-picked columns maximum, count fixed a priori (suggested: area-normalized fert+manure+deposition per km2, tiles13_perc2, ldrainden, CAT_STCLAY), never the full block.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES, with one extra pipeline stage. Values are INCREMENTAL per catchment in kilograms, paired with IncAreaKm2, so for an arbitrary pin you must sum over the NLDI-returned upstream COMID set and divide by CumAreaKm2 to get kg/km2 — raw sums would largely re-encode basin area, which the model already carries as log_basin_area. Mechanically compatible with the existing NLDI delineation step; an accumulation stage, not a lookup.

findings.claim: LEAKAGE TRAP INSIDE THE SPARROW INPUT FILE — do not 'just ingest the table'. Alongside its landscape drivers, mw_sparrow_model_input.txt contains SPARROW's own calibration observations: flux_600_final (monitored TN load; only 522 nonzero of 484,592 rows), flux_665_final (TP, 529 nonzero), flux_530_final (suspended sediment, 388), flux_154_final (65), can_tn_load / can_tp_load / can_ssc_load / can_q_load, mean_dflow_predpd (793), wbm_rhload, iresload, plus four weighting columns (TNAllSN_inv_resid2_hat, TPAllN_inv_resid2_hat, sedN_inv_resid2_hat, flowDN_inv_resid2_hat). These are measured loads at monitoring stations. They are structurally ABSENT at an arbitrary ungauged map pin and present only at the gauged subset, so ingesting all 89 columns would inject observed nitrogen load directly into the feature set at exactly the monitored locations and produce an inflated LOFO number that cannot be reproduced in deployment. This is a far more direct and severe leak than the diffuse coefficient-level circularity discussed elsewhere in this angle. USE AN EXPLICIT WHITELIST of source and landscape columns. Useful byproduct: flux_600_final identifies TN calibration reaches, so it is also the cheapest way to run the calibration-overlap audit.

findings.claim: SPARROW's accuracy degrades exactly at the small-catchment scale that an arbitrary map pin most often lands on, bounding how much any SPARROW-derived feature can help. The report states that 'most of the sites used to calibrate the SPARROW models were located on medium to large streams and may not represent the smallest streams in the Midwest,' that for the TP model 'only 5 percent of the calibration sites were on streams with drainage areas less than about 31 km2; therefore, it is difficult to know how well the model predicted loads in drainages smaller than this,' and that 'caution should be taken when interpreting the finest scale model results (for example, predictions for the individual incremental drainages of the reaches).' ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION, IMPORTANT: the frequently-quoted sentence 'The uncertainty associated with SPARROW predictions is expected to increase for drainage basin sizes smaller than those of stream monitoring sites used to calibrate the model' is NOT in SIR 2019-5114 — the word 'uncertainty' appears exactly once in the entire report, inside a reference title. It is USGS mapper/data-release metadata boilerplate and must not be cited as report text. SCOPE CORRECTION: the 5% / 31 km2 statistic is TP-ONLY. The report gives no equivalent figure for the TN model, so for nitrate the small-basin coverage is UNQUANTIFIED in the source; a similar gap is plausible given TN's comparable calibration n, but it is not documented and the TP number must not be imported. Corroborating in-sample evidence that the small-basin concern is real for TN specifically: unconditioned TN RMSE degrades from 0.39 to 0.65 ln-units for loads below 14 ln-units. Additionally, because catchments average 2.7 km2 while much of the source and landscape data are downscaled county averages, apparent per-reach detail is partly interpolation. PRACTICAL RULE: aggregate SPARROW incremental yield over the whole delineated basin, never use a single outlet reach's incremental value, and expect the feature to be least trustworthy for pins on headwater streams. This predicts a measurable, testable interaction between basin area and any SPARROW-feature gain under LOFO.
findings.effectSize: TP model: only 5% of calibration sites on drainage areas < ~31 km2 (TN equivalent not reported). Unconditioned TN RMSE 0.65 ln-units for loads < 14 ln-units vs 0.39 above. Delivery losses: 14/15/28% of TN/TP/SS lost en route to the Great Lakes, 19/23/52% to the Gulf of Mexico.

findings.claim: SPARROW's spatially constant SOURCE coefficients produce documented regional residual bias, but the risk to Iowa is smaller than a naive reading suggests. Source coefficients are constant across the whole Midwest domain and the authors report that 'relatively large residuals were still identified in the western part of the study area', with residual spatial autocorrelation confirmed (Moran's I 0.199, p=0.0005 for both TN and TP). TWO CORRECTIONS THAT SOFTEN THIS: first, the land-to-water DELIVERY variables in this study ARE spatially varying — only the source coefficients are constant — and the large residuals persisted despite that. Second, and more important for this project, the residual problem is localized to the arid WESTERN part of the study area (Missouri and Arkansas River basins, the Dakotas) where calibration site density is lowest; Iowa sits in the eastern Corn Belt portion where site density is HIGHEST, and the report does not document bias in Iowa specifically. A further mitigating consideration: a smooth regional bias in a SPARROW feature is partly absorbable by an XGBoost model that already carries lat/lon as its #2 and #3 permutation-importance features — so residual regional bias is a reason to expect DIMINISHED MARGINAL VALUE from the feature, not a reason to expect active harm. The report also notes that a Bayesian hierarchical regionally-varying-coefficient SPARROW (Alexander 2015; Strickling & Obenour 2018) was NOT used here and 'could improve their predictability' — i.e. the published product is the spatially-constant-coefficient variant.
findings.effectSize: Residual Moran's I 0.199, p=0.0005; large residuals concentrated in the western study area.
sources: Robertson, D.M., and Saad, D.A., 2019, USGS SIR 2019-5114, https://doi.org/10.3133/sir20195114
findings.feasibilityAtN19: not-applicable — an expectation-setter. The practical read is that the marginal information a SPARROW feature adds beyond existing lat/lon may be small, which is a genuine risk of a null result at 19 folds.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: YES — the bias affects feature quality, not feature availability.

findings.claim: OPERATIONAL GOTCHAS that will silently corrupt or crash a naive ingest of the SPARROW release — all verified by direct file inspection. (1) HTTP RANGE REQUESTS ARE NOT HONORED. ScienceBase ignores the Range header: a request with -r returns HTTP 200 with full content-length and no accept-ranges, not HTTP 206 with a partial body. Any apparent 'range read' success is client-side truncation, and a naive range request pulls the entire 493 MB. Plan on streaming and filtering (curl | awk, accepting a broken pipe) or a full download; you cannot cheaply sample the middle of these files. (2) NEGATIVE COMIDs: the TN output contains 18 negative synthetic reach ids (e.g. -92000151, -92000150) that are SPARROW-internal and will not join to NHDPlusV2 or NLDI. Filter comid > 0 or accept silent join misses. (3) DIVIDE-BY-ZERO: 19 rows in the output have IncAreaKm2 == 0, and ~29,004 rows (2.1%) in the input file do — il_tn/IncAreaKm2 will crash or emit inf. Guard the yield division. (4) NO DATA DICTIONARY: the FGDC metadata XML is listed at size 0 and 404s; ?format=xml returns 415, ?format=fgdc returns 4 bytes. Column units are undocumented in the release and must be taken from the companion report or established empirically. (5) LOG-COLUMN SENTINELS: ldrainden = -11.51292546 = log(1e-5) wherever the underlying value is zero, and ltiles13_perc2 maps zeros to exactly 0.0, which COLLIDES with the legitimate ln(1%) = 0. A tree model will read these as extreme or ambiguous real values. Always ingest the untransformed column plus an explicit is-zero indicator and do your own transform. (6) DEGENERATE-IN-IOWA COLUMNS: aridity is exactly 0 for 99.71% of Iowa catchments (it is a western-region delivery term — drop it), sum_ptsrc_kgn_wwtp is 0 for 99.10% (meaningful only after upstream accumulation), and tiles13_perc2 is 0 for 58.68% of Iowa catchments with median 0 and p90 60.9% — a strongly bimodal pattern consistent with real tiling concentrated in the Des Moines Lobe rather than with missingness, but it means per-catchment tile values look sparse and MUST be area-weighted to basin scale to be informative. (7) LICENSE: the ScienceBase item's rights/rightsStatement field is null. It is a USGS data release and public domain / US Government work in practice, but the release asserts no explicit license string. (8) ACCESS: the ScienceBase HTML page returns HTTP 403 to WebFetch and some clients; the JSON API and direct file GETs work via curl with a browser User-Agent.
findings.effectSize: 18 negative COMIDs and 19 zero-area rows of 1,379,904 output rows; ~29,004 zero-area rows of 484,592 input rows; aridity 99.71% zero in Iowa, sum_ptsrc 99.10% zero, tiles13_perc2 58.68% zero.
sources: Saad, D.A., and Robertson, D.M., 2020, https://doi.org/10.5066/P93QMXC9

findings.claim: THERE IS NO VERIFIED EVIDENCE IN THIS CORPUS THAT INJECTING PROCESS-MODEL OUTPUT AS AN ML INPUT FEATURE IMPROVES UNGAUGED-SITE SKILL. This is the second half of the angle's research question and it came back empty at tier 1. Neither the SPARROW data release nor its parent report contains any evaluation of SPARROW output used as an ML input; that experiment is untested and would have to be run here. The entire process-guided ML literature that would answer the question — Read et al. 2019 on lake-temperature PGDL, Jia et al. 2021 on the Delaware River Basin, Willard et al. 2021 on meta-transfer to unmonitored lakes — reached this synthesis as TIER 3 and was never adversarially verified, so under this project's rules none of its reported effect sizes may warrant a recommendation. Treating that literature strictly as unverified LEADS, the directional signals it offers are cautionary rather than encouraging for this specific project, and each of the following is UNVERIFIED and must not be used as a numeric warrant: the pretraining recipe is reportedly an LSTM weight warm-start that does not port to XGBoost at all (the XGBoost-compatible analogue — process output as an input feature or a base_margin offset — is a variant that literature reportedly never tests); the reported benefit is concentrated in TEMPORAL label scarcity at already-monitored sites, whereas this project is label-rich in time (160,074 site-days) and scarce only in independent SITES; the physics-informed loss term is reportedly the minor contributor relative to pretraining, which matters because a physics loss is far harder to construct for nitrate than for lake energy balance; the one genuinely spatial-holdout study reportedly bought a much smaller gain over simply running the process model at the ungauged site than the within-site experiments suggested, and its source-selection metamodel reportedly requires on the order of 20,000 source-source transfer pairs versus the ~342 available at n=19; and there are reportedly documented cases where transfer or graph components made predictions WORSE than the raw process model for a large minority of targets, and where pretraining on simulations that did not span the test conditions degraded the hybrid below the process model itself. THE HONEST BOTTOM LINE: the recommendation to attach SPARROW-derived static covariates rests entirely on VERIFIED data-availability and data-content findings plus this project's own diagnosis that the deficit is between-site and static. It does NOT rest on any verified demonstration that the technique works. Anyone acting on this angle should expect to be generating the first evidence, not inheriting it.
findings.effectSize: None available at tier 1. All process-guided-ML effect sizes in this corpus are unverified and are deliberately not restated here as warrants.
findings.splitProtocol: N/A — the verified corpus contains no experiment of this kind at any protocol. The unverified leads span temporal-holdout (Read 2019, Jia 2021 main results) and spatial-holdout (Willard 2021; Jia 2021 at n=5 held-out segments) designs; the temporal-holdout numbers would be non-comparable to LOFO 0.820 even if verified.
findings.nBasins: N/A at tier 1. Unverified leads cite 68 lakes / 1 lake (Read), 42 river segments with 5 spatially held out (Jia), and 145 source + 305 target lakes (Willard).
sources: Absence established against: Robertson & Saad 2019, https://doi.org/10.3133/sir20195114; Saad & Robertson 2020, https://doi.org/10.5066/P93QMXC9
UNVERIFIED leads only: Read et al. 2019, https://doi.org/10.1029/2019WR024922; Jia et al. 2021, https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.12575; Willard et al. 2021, https://doi.org/10.1029/2021WR029579
findings.feasibilityAtN19: The cheap variant (add SPARROW-derived static columns to the existing XGBoost, evaluate under LOFO) is feasible at n=19 and costs days. The ambitious variants suggested by the unverified literature are NOT: meta-transfer source selection reportedly needs a metamodel trained on ~20,880 source-source pairs against the ~342 (19x18) available here, roughly 1.6% of that, and a physics-informed loss for nitrate has no established formulation. Do not fund a PGDL rebuild on this evidence.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: The feature-injection variant: YES. The pretraining and fine-tuning variants: NOT DEMONSTRATED at zero local observations — the unverified literature's strongest results reportedly come from regimes with at least a few local labels at the target, which is precisely what an arbitrary Iowa map pin does not have.

findings.claim: The Iowa Nutrient Reduction Strategy appears NOT to be a viable source of per-reach process-model output, which removes one of the three sub-targets of this angle. UNVERIFIED: the 2013 NRS science assessment reportedly does not use a calibrated process model at all (not SWAT, not SPARROW, not EPIC/APEX) for the statewide nitrate baseline, instead applying a GIS spreadsheet method built on universal nitrogen-response curves relating subsurface nitrate concentration to N application rate, with nitrate yield as the product of concentration and water yield; and reportedly reports all results at the Major Land Resource Area scale, of which Iowa contains only EIGHT — meaning there is no per-NHDPlus-reach and no per-catchment output, and an NRS-derived feature could be no finer than an 8-category regional lookup, near-collinear with the lat/lon features already ranked #2 and #3 in permutation importance. Also UNVERIFIED and consistent with this: the NRS reportedly concedes its own MLRA-scale N inputs are too coarse to represent real between-site variation, that its application rates rest on possibly outdated data, and that its water-yield submodel is a 1981-2010 climatology on a 300 m grid with no daily resolution; and its reported validation statistic (a 'prediction efficiency' of 82.5% against 26 Iowa stations after a +17% bias correction estimated from those same 26 stations) is reportedly an in-sample fit with no held-out basins, hence not comparable to LOFO 0.820 and itself a circularity exposure. ALL OF THE ABOVE IS UNVERIFIED and is offered as a lead for a cheap confirmation, not as a warrant. If confirmed, the practical conclusion is to drop the NRS branch of this angle entirely and concentrate on SPARROW. One unverified but interesting mechanistic byproduct worth a look regardless: the NRS reportedly asserts that in tile-drained Iowa landscapes surface runoff carries negligible nitrate (<1 mg/L) and that rain events therefore DILUTE in-stream concentrations, competing against a delayed tile-flushing enrichment effect — which, if true, is a documented mechanistic explanation for why this project's same-day scalar precipitation feature carries near-zero permutation importance (precip_in_1d perm ~0.000).
findings.effectSize: UNVERIFIED: published output resolution reportedly 8 MLRA regions statewide, 0 per-reach units.
findings.splitProtocol: UNVERIFIED; reportedly in-sample with no held-out basins.
findings.nBasins: UNVERIFIED: reportedly 8 MLRAs as reporting units; 26 Iowa river watersheds in the reported validation; 38 gauged watersheds in the water-yield regression.
sources: UNVERIFIED: Iowa Nutrient Reduction Strategy science assessment (2013), https://publications.iowa.gov/23225/1/NRSfull-130529.pdf
findings.feasibilityAtN19: If the MLRA-only resolution is confirmed, INFEASIBLE as a between-site feature regardless of n — 8 categories across 19 families, near-collinear with lat/lon, cannot add independent between-site signal. The n=19 constraint is not even the binding limitation; spatial resolution is.
findings.worksAtUngaugedPin: Mechanically yes (an 8-region lookup is defined everywhere in Iowa), but almost certainly worthless — it would add no information beyond the lat/lon the model already leans on heavily, and it does not extend to the multi-state portions of Iowa basins.

datasets.name: SPARROW Midwest 2012 model INPUT attributes (mw_sparrow_model_input.txt), within USGS data release 'SPARROW model inputs and simulated streamflow, nutrient and suspended-sediment loads in streams of the Midwestern United States, 2012 Base Year' (Saad & Robertson 2020)
datasets.url: https://doi.org/10.5066/P93QMXC9 — direct file GET via https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/file/get/5cbf5150e4b09b8c0b700df3?f=<pathOnDisk>, enumerate pathOnDisk from https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/item/5cbf5150e4b09b8c0b700df3?format=json
datasets.resolution: One row per NHDPlusV2 incremental catchment (ComID key), mean catchment 2.7 km2, median ~1.4 km2. 89 columns, ~484,592 rows, 740 MB comma-delimited text. NOTE: effective resolution of several agricultural columns is coarser than the catchment implies — the report states much of the source and landscape data derive from county-wide averages apportioned to catchments by fine-scale land use.
datasets.years: Single static 2012 base year (source terms); hydrology normalized to long-term average over 1999/2000-2014. Tile layer is circa-2012 (Nakagaki & Wieczorek 2016) despite the '13' in the column name. NO temporal dimension whatsoever.
datasets.access: Free bulk HTTP GET, no authentication, no registration, no API key, no rate limit. Range requests are NOT honored (server returns 200 with full content-length), so stream-and-filter or download in full. ScienceBase HTML pages 403 some clients; use the JSON API and a browser User-Agent.
datasets.license: USGS data release; ScienceBase rights/rightsStatement field is NULL — public domain / US Government work in practice, but no explicit license string is asserted by the release.
datasets.coversMultiState: YES — populated across the entire Midwest model domain (Mississippi, Great Lakes, Red River of the North basins), including MN, SD, NE, MO, WI, IL. This directly repairs the project's documented inner-join defect where basins extending outside Iowa silently under-count crop area and N surplus. The tile-drainage column specifically derives from a 12-state layer (SD, NE, KS, MN, IA, MO, WI, IL, MI, IN, OH, KY) which encompasses every out-of-state upstream portion of an Iowa basin.
datasets.whyUseful: The single highest-value item in this angle. It closes the project's stated tile-drainage gap outright, and it supplies complete, multi-state, gap-free 2012 nitrogen source terms that supplement the gTREND N-surplus product that ends in 2017 and is NaN for 68% of training rows. Every column is a STATIC per-basin quantity, which is exactly the shape of the project's diagnosed deficit (between_r2 0.21 vs within_r2 0.42) and the only feature class that has historically produced wins here.
datasets.howToIncorporate: Whitelist 3-5 columns; do NOT ingest the block. Pipeline: map pin -> NLDI upstream COMID list -> join on ComID (filter comid > 0 and IncAreaKm2 > 0). Create: (1) `basin_tile_frac` = area-weighted mean of tiles13_perc2 over upstream catchments, weights = IncAreaKm2 — use the RAW column and do your own transform, because ltiles13_perc2 maps zeros to exactly 0.0 which collides with ln(1%)=0; (2) `basin_n_input_kg_km2` = (sum of ManN2012 + fert_sw_N_kg + cmaq_TN_12_kg over upstream catchments) / CumAreaKm2 — divide by area or the raw sum merely re-encodes basin size, already present as log_basin_area; (3) `basin_drainden` = area-weighted mean of ldrainden, remapping the sentinel -11.51292546 (= log(1e-5), meaning zero) to a real zero plus an is-zero indicator; (4) `basin_clay` = area-weighted mean of CAT_STCLAY. Broadcast each as a single time-invariant value across all site-days for that basin — NEVER as a time-varying column, which reproduces the failed 2017-surplus-broadcast ablation (lofo_r2 -0.166). Fix the column count a priori rather than selecting on LOFO score.
datasets.limitations: STATIC 2012 SNAPSHOT — supplements but cannot substitute for a time-varying N surplus; it replaces a 68%-NaN series with a constant, removing temporal variation rather than restoring it. LEAKAGE TRAP: the file also contains flux_600_final / flux_665_final / flux_530_final / flux_154_final / can_*_load / mean_dflow_predpd / *_inv_resid2_hat — monitoring-derived calibration loads present only at gauged reaches and structurally absent at an ungauged pin; ingesting them would inflate LOFO. DEGENERATE IN IOWA: aridity 99.71% zero, sum_ptsrc_kgn_wwtp 99.10% zero, tiles13_perc2 58.68% zero (bimodal, consistent with real Des Moines Lobe tiling, but requires basin-scale area weighting to be informative). Values are INCREMENTAL per catchment, never pre-accumulated. Tile layer is a MODELED estimate from land cover, soils and slope (ND/SD are permit polygons, a non-comparable construction), not a tile inventory — errors are spatially structured, the worst kind for a between-site predictor. Column casing is inconsistent (ComID mixed, huc12 lowercase and blank for some rows). No units documentation: the FGDC XML is size 0 and 404s. n=19: aggregating to basins collapses these to ~19 effective units, and the county-average provenance means within-family variation is near-constant — high overfitting risk if more than a handful of columns are added.

datasets.name: SPARROW Midwest 2012 model OUTPUT — total nitrogen (mw_sparrow_model_output_TN.txt), same data release
datasets.resolution: One row per NHDPlusV2 COMID, 1,379,904 rows x 40 columns, 493 MB plain CSV. Companion files: _TP.txt (446 MB), _SS.txt (501 MB), _FLOW.txt (270 MB), mw_reach.zip (802 MB reach network), mw_cats.zip (600 MB catchment polygons). ~3.85 GB total across 7 data files (the item lists an 8th, a broken metadata XML).
datasets.years: Long-term mean-annual, base year 2012, hydrology detrended/normalized over 1999/2000-2014. ZERO temporal resolution — the report states its results 'enable model results to be used to rank areas based on their typical losses of a specific constituent; however, this feature does not allow areas to be ranked during any specific year or season.'
datasets.access: Free bulk HTTP GET, no authentication. Range requests NOT honored — stream and truncate, or download in full.
datasets.license: USGS data release; rights field null — public domain / US Government work in practice, no explicit license string asserted.
datasets.coversMultiState: YES — Mississippi, Great Lakes and Red River of the North basins, ~1.36M catchments, covering all of Iowa and every out-of-state upstream portion of Iowa basins.
datasets.whyUseful: Supplies a per-reach 'expected absolute nitrogen level' — precisely the between-site quantity the model cannot currently rank ('a good timer, a mediocre site-ranker'). Both incremental and accumulated loads are published, with seven-way source attribution and per-reach standard errors, so the feature can encode not just how loaded a basin is but WHY (fertilizer vs manure vs point source vs atmospheric).
datasets.howToIncorporate: Join on the NLDI-returned upstream COMID set (filter comid > 0; guard IncAreaKm2 == 0, which occurs in 19 rows). Create at most 3 static per-basin columns: (1) `sparrow_inc_tn_yield` = sum(il_tn) / sum(IncAreaKm2) over upstream catchments, i.e. locally-generated TN yield in kg/km2/yr; (2) `sparrow_dominant_source_share` = the largest of il_tn_fert / il_tn_man / il_tn_atm / il_tn_wwtp as a fraction of il_tn, aggregated basin-wide, or the fertilizer+manure share as a single scalar; (3) `sparrow_del_frac` = area-weighted mean DEL_FRAC at the outlet reach. Broadcast each as a time-invariant value across all site-days. A derived mean-annual concentration from al_tn and wbm_meanq is possible but confirm units first (empirically kg/yr and cfs; not documented in the release) — a unit error is a harmless constant for a tree split but ruins interpretation.
datasets.limitations: Static mean-annual TN LOAD, not daily nitrate concentration — carries no temporal signal and cannot help the WHEN question, which is already the model's strength. Nitrate is only a fraction of total nitrogen, and treating that fraction as stable across Iowa tile-drained basins is an UNTESTED assumption. The released product is UNCONDITIONED simulated load (correct for ungauged use, but the lower-accuracy variant). Small-basin accuracy is poor and the report explicitly cautions against using individual incremental-reach predictions. Regional residual bias exists (Moran's I 0.199, p=0.0005) though concentrated in the arid west rather than Iowa. Circularity is diffuse (~1/1,334 per-site leverage on global coefficients) but the calibration-overlap audit should be run once before publishing a LOFO gain. n=19: expect wide error bars; pre-register a <0.03 PR-AUC gain as a null.

datasets.name: Estimates of subsurface tile drainage extent for 12 Midwest states, 2012 (Nakagaki, N., and Wieczorek, M.E., 2016) — the source layer behind SPARROW's tile column
datasets.resolution: UNVERIFIED as to native raster resolution (reported as 30 m, built from 2012 Census of Agriculture state-level tiled acreage + NLCD 2011 cultivated cropland + STATSGO2 poorly/moderately drained soils). VERIFIED: it is already pre-aggregated to NHDPlusV2 catchments (mean 2.7 km2) as tiles13_perc2 inside mw_sparrow_model_input.txt, which is the far easier access route.
datasets.years: Circa-2012 single static snapshot. ND/SD supplemented from tile-permit polygons (ND 2016, SD 2012).
datasets.access: Free bulk download from ScienceBase, no authentication.
datasets.coversMultiState: YES for the practical purpose — 12 Midwest states: SD, NE, KS, MN, IA, MO, WI, IL, MI, IN, OH, KY. This encompasses all of Iowa and every out-of-state upstream portion of Iowa basins. It would NOT cover a basin extending into North Dakota outside the permit-polygon supplement. NOTE: the SPARROW release's bounding box (-114.85 to -72.51 lon) and 30+ place tags are NHDPlusV2 network metadata artifacts and are NOT evidence of tile-layer coverage — cite the 12-state extent instead.
datasets.whyUseful: Closes the project's explicitly stated gap: 'Tile drainage density: known to be the dominant hydrologic control in Iowa, NOT in the feature set, and NO data source has been identified yet.' A source now exists.
datasets.howToIncorporate: Do NOT process the raster. Take tiles13_perc2 from mw_sparrow_model_input.txt via COMID join (see that dataset's entry) — same values, no geoprocessing. Optionally check whether a tile-drainage member of the Wieczorek et al. NHDPlus 'Select Attributes' series exists in pre-accumulated CAT/ACC/TOT form, which would avoid streaming a 740 MB file for two columns; a keyword search for one returned 0 hits but that is likely a query-syntax issue rather than proof of absence, and it is worth ten minutes before committing to the large parse.
datasets.limitations: MODELED ESTIMATE, NOT AN INVENTORY — derived from downscaled state-level census acreage apportioned by soil and land cover; errors are spatially structured. ND/SD permit polygons are a different and non-comparable construction. Single static vintage, no temporal signal. AND THE EXPECTATION MUST BE MANAGED: SPARROW's own fit gives ln(tile %) the WEAKEST significant land-to-water coefficient in the TN model (0.101 vs ln(runoff) 0.673), a ~7.3% delivery increase per doubling — the project's 'dominant hydrologic control' prior is not supported. Tile extent in Iowa is also strongly spatially structured and will correlate with lat/lon, already the #2 and #3 features, so marginal gain may be near zero.

datasets.name: SPARROW Midwest 2012 ArcGIS REST MapServer (interactive/queryable alternative to bulk download)
datasets.resolution: UNVERIFIED: reportedly 43 layers — 36 polygon layers (9 each for tn, tp, q, ss), 4 calibration-site point layers (IDs 36-39), 3 line layers. The TN catchment polygon layer is reportedly layer 9 (mw_cats_tn), keyed by COMID, reportedly carrying CONCENTRAT (mean-annual TN concentration), INCL/ACCL (incremental/accumulated load), INCY/ACCY (yields), delivered variants DINCL/DACCL/DINCY/DACCY, DEL_FRAC, and per-source decompositions ACCL_S1-S7.
datasets.years: Same 2012 base year as the bulk release.
datasets.access: UNVERIFIED: reportedly a public ArcGIS REST endpoint supporting where=, returnCountOnly=, geometry= and standard ArcGIS query parameters, with no authentication. Also reportedly an interactive subsetting UI exporting CSV/Excel/geospatial by state, HUC or catchment.
datasets.license: Same USGS public-domain status as the bulk release.
datasets.coversMultiState: YES (same domain as the bulk release).
datasets.whyUseful: UNVERIFIED LEAD, useful for two things the bulk files make awkward: (a) a CONCENTRAT field would be a mean-annual TN concentration, the closest published analogue to the absolute level this model cannot rank, without needing to derive it from load and flow with undocumented units; (b) the calibration-site point layers would make the circularity audit a spatial query rather than a document exercise. A reported bounding-box query over Iowa returned 110 TN calibration sites, and the layer reportedly carries STATION_ID and STATION_NM.
datasets.howToIncorporate: For the audit (the more valuable use): query the TN calibration-site layer over the Iowa bounding box, then join STATION_ID / coordinates against the 85 site identifiers with a distance tolerance — COMID-exact matching alone will under-detect, since the report permits a WQ site up to 40 km from its paired gauge. Report how many of the 19 FAMILIES contain at least one calibration site, and report LOFO both on all 19 and restricted to non-overlapping families. For features, prefer the bulk files; a REST call per basin is not a sensible ingest path for 85 basins x thousands of COMIDs.
datasets.limitations: ENTIRELY UNVERIFIED — layer numbering, field names and the 110-site Iowa count were extracted but never adversarially checked, so confirm the schema before building anything on it. Same substantive limitations as the bulk product (static, mean-annual, load-not-nitrate, poor on small basins). Note also that the frequently-quoted 'uncertainty ... is expected to increase for drainage basin sizes smaller than those of stream monitoring sites' sentence originates from this mapper/metadata layer, NOT from SIR 2019-5114 — do not cite it as report text.

datasets.name: Select Attributes for NHDPlus Version 2.1 Reach Catchments and Modified Network Routed Upstream Watersheds for the Conterminous United States (Wieczorek, Jackson, Schwarz, Sekellick & Staub)
datasets.url: https://doi.org/10.5066/F7765D7V — child items enumerable on ScienceBase; parquet files reportedly at https://prod-is-usgs-sb-prod-publish.s3.amazonaws.com/<itemid>/<itemid>_{cat,acc,tot}.parquet
datasets.resolution: UNVERIFIED: reportedly ~2.7 million NHDPlusV2 stream segments, keyed by COMID (flowline ComID / catchment FEATUREID), delivered in three routings — _cat (local reach catchment), _acc (divergence-routed accumulation), _tot (total cumulative upstream drainage). 158 child theme items across 13 themes.
datasets.years: UNVERIFIED: reportedly spans 1870-2020 across themes; individual attributes are single-vintage snapshots. Release 2018, revised through June 2025.
datasets.access: UNVERIFIED: reportedly anonymous HTTP GET from a public S3 bucket, no credentials, no API key (an HTTP 206 with valid PAR1 parquet magic bytes was reportedly observed). IMPORTANT UNVERIFIED NEGATIVE RESULT: the USGS NLDI characteristics endpoints reportedly returned HTTP 404 (both /nldi/linked-data/characteristics/tot and /nldi/linked-data/comid/<comid>/tot), so although this project already calls NLDI for delineation, it reportedly CANNOT pull these attributes in the same call — the working pattern would be to pre-download the parquet tables once and join locally on the NLDI-returned COMID set.
datasets.license: USGS data release, public domain / unrestricted use.
datasets.coversMultiState: YES — conterminous United States, so no Iowa-boundary clipping artifact at all.
datasets.whyUseful: UNVERIFIED LEAD, but potentially the cleanest access route in this angle. If the _tot (pre-accumulated upstream) routing exists for the attributes of interest, it eliminates the area-weighted aggregation step entirely — the upstream-accumulated value is a direct COMID lookup at the outlet. Reportedly relevant child items include tile drainage (Nakagaki early-1990s, id 58d9dec6e4b0543bf7fda70e, columns COMID / TOT_TILES_Early90s / TOT_TILES_Early90s_NODATA), an independent NRI-606 1992 tile estimate (id 57067469e4b03f95a075ad3e) permitting a cross-check, field-ditch surface drainage (id 57067257e4b03f95a075ab0c), and 2012 fertilizer/manure N and P (id 59038bc8e4b0e862d2311aef, Brakebill et al. 2017 and Gronberg et al. 2017, units kilograms).
datasets.howToIncorporate: Pre-download the _tot parquet for 2-4 chosen attributes once; at prediction time, look up the outlet COMID directly to get the upstream-accumulated value with no aggregation code. Candidate features mirror the SPARROW ones: basin tile percentage, basin fertilizer+manure N per km2. If both this and the SPARROW input file supply tile drainage, run them against each other — disagreement between the Nakagaki early-1990s and NRI-606 1992 products bounds the measurement error of any tile feature, which is worth knowing before attributing a LOFO change to it.
datasets.limitations: ENTIRELY UNVERIFIED — item IDs, column names, the S3 URL pattern and the NLDI 404 all need confirming before an ingest is planned. VINTAGE MISMATCH: the tile products here are early-1990s and 1992, roughly two decades older than SPARROW's circa-2012 layer, and Iowa tiling has changed since; prefer the 2012 layer and use these only as a cross-check. CIRCULARITY IS MOSTLY ABSENT HERE, which is a genuine advantage: most items are landscape descriptors derived from census, remote-sensing and soils data with no nitrate observation involved. ONE EXCEPTION reportedly carries both circularity and downscaling problems — the NRCS Best Management Practice scenarios item (id 5cc89237e4b09b8c0b77f247), reportedly APEX-simulated and SWAT-extrapolated, and reportedly available natively only at HUC2 scale before being 'extended to the NHDPlus version 2.1 catchment scale' by geospatial techniques, meaning its apparent per-catchment detail is largely interpolation artifact; it also reportedly states it was built 'for use in the SPARROW models'. Avoid that item, or test first whether it varies within a HUC2 only as a function of land-cover weights.

datasets.name: SPARROW calibration-target dataset (Saad et al. 2019) — water-quality and streamflow datasets used to estimate the long-term loads SPARROW was fit to
datasets.url: https://doi.org/10.5066/F7DN436B (data release); companion report Saad et al. 2019, USGS SIR 2019-5069, https://doi.org/10.3133/sir20195069
datasets.resolution: UNVERIFIED: reportedly DISCRETE MONITORING-SITE POINT LOCATIONS only — long-term mean daily streamflow and detrended long-term mean annual TN, TP and suspended-sediment loads at roughly 3,300 nutrient sites nationally, 1,344 TN in the Midwest. NOT reach-mapped.
datasets.years: 1999-10-01 to 2014-09-30 compilation window; loads detrended to a 2012 base year (pivoted around 2012.5). Streamflow reportedly NOT detrended, the authors judging a 15-year record too short.
datasets.access: UNVERIFIED: reportedly free bulk download from ScienceBase, no authentication.
datasets.coversMultiState: N/A — point locations, not a coverage.
datasets.whyUseful: NOT a feature source. Its value to this project is exactly one thing: it is the table against which to run the circularity audit. Because values exist only at monitored points, it CANNOT be joined to an arbitrary ungauged map pin and is useless as a deployment feature.
datasets.howToIncorporate: Audit only. Join this project's 85 site coordinates/COMIDs against the site table with a distance tolerance, count how many of the 19 basin families contain a TN calibration site, and report LOFO gains both overall and on non-overlapping families. Do not create any model feature from it.
datasets.limitations: UNVERIFIED throughout. Reportedly, the loads themselves carry large stated uncertainty even after screening — retained only if the standard error was within 50% of the mean load estimate, with an acceptable bias ratio of 0.66 to 1.5 — which if true implies any SPARROW-derived feature inherits an error floor of order +/-50% on its underlying calibration targets, so a downstream ML gain smaller than that noise band should not be attributed to real process information. Also reportedly, small ungauged headwaters are under-represented by construction: the streamgage-matching requirement alone eliminated 53% of otherwise-qualifying Midwest sites (3,137 -> 1,470), biasing calibration density toward larger gauged basins — i.e. toward exactly the opposite of this project's deployment target.

datasets.name: Iowa Nutrient Reduction Strategy science assessment (2013)
datasets.resolution: UNVERIFIED: reportedly 8 MLRA regions statewide, with NO per-reach or per-catchment output. A companion water-yield product is reportedly a 300 m kriged grid but represents a 1981-2010 climatology only.
datasets.years: UNVERIFIED: 2013 assessment; water-yield submodel reportedly 1981-2010; N application rates reportedly based on Blackmer et al. 1997.
datasets.access: Free PDF download, no authentication. No structured data product identified.
datasets.coversMultiState: NO — Iowa only. It cannot describe the out-of-state upstream portions of multi-state Iowa basins, which is one of this project's known defects.
datasets.whyUseful: Marginal at best. Included for completeness because the angle names it explicitly. If the MLRA-only resolution is confirmed, its only residual value is mechanistic rather than as a feature: reportedly-stated statewide constants (17% surface / 83% subsurface water yield, surface runoff nitrate <1 mg/L, nonpoint sources 92% of TN) offer a physical explanation for why this project's same-day precipitation features are dead — rain dilutes in-stream concentration on the day while enriching it later via tile flushing, two competing signs that net to near-zero permutation importance.
datasets.howToIncorporate: Do not build a feature from it. If anything, use the reported dilution-versus-flushing mechanism as a hypothesis generator for why same-day precipitation fails — though note that lagged and routed weather have ALREADY been tried here and hurt badly (loso_r2 0.116 -> 0.019), so this mechanistic story does not obviously license another attempt.
datasets.limitations: UNVERIFIED throughout, and if the resolution claim holds, disqualifying: 8 categories across 19 basin families, near-collinear with lat/lon which are already the #2 and #3 features. Reportedly not a calibrated process model at all but a GIS spreadsheet method on universal nitrogen-response curves. Its reported validation (82.5% prediction efficiency at 26 Iowa stations, after a +17% bias correction estimated from those same 26 stations) is reportedly in-sample with no held-out basins — not comparable to LOFO 0.820, and a circularity exposure in its own right. The document reportedly concedes its MLRA-scale inputs are too coarse to capture real between-site variation, which is the exact failure this project is trying to fix.

refuted.claim: Tile drainage density is 'the dominant hydrologic control in Iowa' — stated as an assumption in the project brief.
refuted.correction: NOT SUPPORTED by the best available calibrated fit. In the Midwest SPARROW TN model, ln(tile drains, % of catchment) carries coefficient 0.101 — statistically strong (p<0.0001, t=4.5, VIF 2.3) but the WEAKEST significant land-to-water delivery term in the model. The same table gives ln(runoff) 0.673, ln(soil clay) 0.292, ln(no-till) 0.124. In log-space elasticity terms runoff dominates tile drainage by roughly 7x, and doubling tile percentage raises modeled TN delivery only ~7.3%. Tile drainage carries real, independent between-catchment nitrogen information; it is not the dominant control. Expect a small between-site contribution, not a fix for between_r2 0.21.

refuted.claim: SPARROW output at a monitored reach 'partly encodes that site's own observed level', making a SPARROW feature severely leaky under LOFO.
refuted.correction: OVERSTATED; the mechanism does not work that way. Load-substitution ('conditioning') is applied during calibration and to the calibration RMSE, NOT to the distributed reach predictions. The public data release ships ONLY unconditioned simulated loads, and the output files contain no station ID, no measured load and no residual — a reach's published value is a deterministic function of catchment attributes and ~14-15 globally shared coefficients, computed identically at monitored and unmonitored reaches. A single Iowa site's observations enter as roughly 1/1,334 of a Midwest-wide coefficient fit, further downweighted by the report's nested-share scheme. Target mismatch compounds the dilution: even a fully contaminated reach would leak a slow basin-average annual LOAD level, never a daily 10 mg/L label. The audit remains cheap insurance at only 19 folds, but this is not the severe site-level leak it was framed as. NOTE: a genuinely severe leak DOES exist in the input file's flux_*_final columns — see the corresponding finding; that one is real and must be guarded against.

refuted.claim: SIR 2019-5114 states that 'The uncertainty associated with SPARROW predictions is expected to increase for drainage basin sizes smaller than those of stream monitoring sites used to calibrate the model.'
refuted.correction: MISATTRIBUTED. This sentence is NOT in SIR 2019-5114 — the word 'uncertainty' appears exactly once in the entire report, inside a reference title. It is USGS mapper / data-release metadata boilerplate. The report's actual wording for the small-basin caveat is: 'most of the sites used to calibrate the SPARROW models were located on medium to large streams and may not represent the smallest streams in the Midwest ... it is difficult to know how well the model predicted loads in drainages smaller than this ... caution should be taken when interpreting the finest scale model results (for example, predictions for the individual incremental drainages of the reaches).' The substantive limitation is real; only the quotation is wrong.

refuted.claim: The '5 percent of calibration sites below ~31 km2' statistic characterizes SPARROW's small-basin coverage for nitrogen.
refuted.correction: SCOPE ERROR — that figure is TOTAL PHOSPHORUS ONLY. The report gives no equivalent small-basin statistic for the TN model. Since this project's target is nitrate, the honest statement is that TN small-basin calibration coverage is UNQUANTIFIED in the source. A similar gap is plausible given TN's comparable calibration n, but it is not documented and the TP number must not be imported. Independent in-sample evidence that the concern is real for TN: unconditioned TN RMSE degrades from 0.39 to 0.65 ln-units for loads below 14 ln-units.

refuted.claim: SPARROW's spatially constant coefficients imply systematic regional bias 'that would propagate into any feature built from SPARROW output', including in Iowa.
refuted.correction: OVERREACHED. Only the SOURCE coefficients are spatially constant; the land-to-water DELIVERY variables in this study are spatially varying. The report locates its large residuals in the arid WESTERN part of the study area (Missouri and Arkansas River basins, the Dakotas) where calibration site density is lowest, and documents no bias in Iowa specifically — Iowa sits in the eastern Corn Belt portion where site density is highest. Further, a smooth regional bias is partly absorbable by an XGBoost model that already carries lat/lon as its #2 and #3 features, so the realistic consequence is DIMINISHED MARGINAL VALUE from the feature, not active harm.

refuted.claim: SPARROW's Yield R2 of 0.913 is a meaningful reference point for this project's between_r2 of 0.21, and R2 0.950 is inflated mainly because accumulated load is dominated by drainage area.
refuted.correction: BOTH HALVES NEED FIXING. The drainage-area argument is directionally right but does not carry the case: Yield R2 = 0.913 IS area-normalized (kg/km2/yr) and still high, so area dominance alone cannot explain it. The sufficient and much stronger grounds for non-comparability are (a) all four statistics are in-sample calibration fit with NO spatial holdout anywhere in the 74-page report, with confirmed residual spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I 0.199, p=0.0005); (b) the response variable is long-term mean-annual TN LOAD in kg/yr, not daily-max nitrate concentration exceedance; (c) SPARROW is steady-state with no time dimension at all; and (d) Yield R2 is a cross-sectional fit across a continental domain where yields span orders of magnitude, whereas between_r2 is across 19 Iowa corn-belt families with a severely restricted range. The two numbers are not on the same axis in any sense, and no rescaling makes SPARROW's RMSE a benchmark for LOFO AUC 0.820.

refuted.claim: Header verification of the ScienceBase files was performed 'by HTTP range request'.
refuted.correction: The server does NOT honor Range. A request with -r returns HTTP 200 with the full content-length and no accept-ranges header, delivering the file from byte 0; any apparent success is client-side truncation of a streamed full GET. Substantively immaterial — the headers reported are correct — but the method does not do what it says, and a naive range request will pull the entire 493 MB. Practical consequence: you cannot cheaply sample the middle of these files; stream-and-filter or download in full.

refuted.claim: The Midwest SPARROW TN model is 'a 16-parameter regression'.
refuted.correction: Table 5 lists 17 model TERMS. Three are fixed/specified rather than fitted (Canada load = 1.0; public-supply surface-water withdrawal = 1.0; groundwater-irrigation pumping loss = 1.221 — all three carry '--' for standard error, p-value and t-value), leaving 14-15 freely estimated coefficients depending on how one counts. Correct phrasing: 'a 17-variable regression with 14-15 freely calibrated coefficients'. This sharpens rather than weakens the n=19 argument: a sites-to-estimated-parameters ratio near 95:1 is a model structure that 19 independent basin families could not support at all.

refuted.claim: Incidental site counts: '1,346 TN sites considered', '107 suspended sediment calibration sites', 'a 60-page report'.
refuted.correction: All three are wrong, though none is load-bearing. Table 1 assigns 1,344 considered / 1,335 used to TOTAL NITROGEN and 1,346 to TOTAL PHOSPHORUS — the report's own narrative text transposes TN and TP here, so the source is internally inconsistent and should be cited as such. Table 5 says 1,334 TN, a further one-site disagreement with Table 1; 1,334 is the operative calibration n. The suspended-sediment model used 1,185 sites, not 107 — an order-of-magnitude error. The TP model's Table 7 reports 1,271 against Table 1's 1,273. The report is 74 p. including 5 appendixes (88 PDF pages), not 60. The 'no cross-validation anywhere' finding holds across all 88 pages.

refuted.claim: The tile-drainage layer is a 'circa-2013' snapshot, and the SPARROW release's bounding box and place tags demonstrate its coverage.
refuted.correction: TWO ERRORS, RIGHT CONCLUSION. The vintage is circa-2012 — the source is Nakagaki & Wieczorek's 2012-base-year product built from the 2012 Census of Agriculture, NLCD 2011, and STATSGO2; the '13' in TILES13_PERC2 is a variable-naming artifact, not the data year. And the bounding box (-114.85 to -72.51 lon, 27.66 to 50.15 lat) plus 30+ place tags including Virginia, New Mexico and Texas are metadata artifacts of the NHDPlusV2 network extent, NOT evidence of tile-layer coverage. The tile layer covers 12 Midwest states only (SD, NE, KS, MN, IA, MO, WI, IL, MI, IN, OH, KY, plus ND/SD permit polygons). The operative conclusion survives — all of Iowa and every upstream state Iowa basins reach are inside those 12 — but it must be justified by the 12-state extent, not the bbox.

refuted.claim: The SPARROW model input file is '~85 columns' and is 'directly ingestible by an ML model'.
refuted.correction: 89 columns, and 'directly ingestible' is dangerous if applied to all of them. The file contains SPARROW's own calibration observations — flux_600_final, flux_665_final, flux_530_final, flux_154_final, can_*_load, mean_dflow_predpd, wbm_rhload, iresload, and four *_inv_resid2_hat weighting terms — which are measured loads present only at gauged reaches and structurally absent at an ungauged pin. Ingesting the full file would inject observed nitrogen load into the features at exactly the monitored locations and inflate LOFO. Use an explicit whitelist of source and landscape columns. Also: the join key is ComID (mixed case), huc12 is lowercase and blank for some rows, and ~29,004 rows (2.1%) have IncAreaKm2 = 0 with many carrying negative synthetic ComIDs.

uncovered: THE CENTRAL QUESTION OF THIS ANGLE IS UNANSWERED AT TIER 1. No verified source in this corpus evaluates whether injecting process-model output as an INPUT FEATURE to an ML model improves ungauged-site skill — for nitrate or for anything else. The SPARROW data release and its parent report contain no such experiment, and the entire process-guided ML literature reached this synthesis unverified. Under this angle's rules, that literature can name the technique but cannot warrant it. The recommendation to attach SPARROW-derived static covariates therefore rests on data availability, data content, and this project's own between-site diagnosis — NOT on any verified demonstration that the technique works. Acting on it means generating the first evidence.

NO VERIFIED PROCESS-GUIDED ML EVIDENCE OF ANY KIND. Read et al. (2019), Jia et al. (2021) and Willard et al. (2021) — the three papers the angle explicitly asks about, covering pretraining on process-model output, physics-informed loss terms, and meta-transfer learning to unmonitored sites — are all tier 3. Their reported effect sizes, split protocols and basin counts are unverified and are deliberately not used as warrants anywhere in this synthesis. Verifying even one of them would materially change the confidence attached to this angle, and is the highest-value follow-up available.

NO VERIFIED EVIDENCE ON WHETHER SPARROW-DERIVED FEATURES ACTUALLY MOVE between_r2 OR between_rate_r2. The claim that a static per-basin nitrogen-level covariate is 'the right shape' for this project's deficit is an inference from the project's own diagnostics, not a published result. It is falsifiable and cheap to test: add area-weighted SPARROW incremental TN yield plus basin tile fraction, re-run LOFO, and check whether the gain concentrates in the between-site terms with little change in within_r2. Nobody has run this.

EPIC / APEX / SWAT IOWA APPLICATIONS PRODUCED NOTHING USABLE. The angle explicitly asks for these. The only trace in the entire corpus is an unverified mention of an NRCS BMP-scenario product that is reportedly APEX-simulated and SWAT-extrapolated but reportedly available natively only at HUC2 scale before being spread down to catchments by geospatial techniques — which would make its apparent per-catchment detail an interpolation artifact. No Iowa-specific SWAT or EPIC/APEX application with publicly downloadable per-reach or per-catchment nitrogen output was identified at any tier. This is a genuine gap, not a null result: the search may simply have missed it.

NO PUBLISHED GRIDDED NITROGEN-LEACHING PRODUCT WAS FOUND. The angle asks for one explicitly. Nothing at tier 1 or tier 3 identifies a gridded N-leaching dataset covering Iowa. Reported as absence of evidence.

THE IOWA NRS ASSESSMENT IS ENTIRELY UNVERIFIED. Every claim about it — the MLRA-only resolution that would disqualify it, the GIS-spreadsheet rather than process-model method, the 82.5% in-sample prediction efficiency, the statewide flow-partitioning constants — arrived at tier 3. The MLRA-resolution finding is the load-bearing one and is worth a single cheap confirmation, since if true it closes the NRS branch of this angle outright.

THE CALIBRATION-OVERLAP AUDIT HAS NOT BEEN RUN. It is not known how many of this project's 85 sites, or of its 19 basin families, contain a SPARROW TN calibration site. An unverified bounding-box query reportedly returned 110 TN calibration sites in or near Iowa out of 1,334 Midwest-wide, but the overlap with the 85 is undetermined. The verified analysis indicates the leakage mechanism is diffuse enough that this is insurance rather than a blocker — but at only 19 folds it should still be measured before any LOFO gain is published.

UNITS FOR THE SPARROW OUTPUT COLUMNS ARE NOT AUTHORITATIVELY DOCUMENTED. The release's FGDC metadata XML is listed at size 0 and 404s; ?format=xml returns 415. Units were established empirically as kg/yr for load columns and cfs for wbm_meanq, cross-checked against physically plausible derived concentrations, but this is inference, not documentation. Confirm against SIR 2019-5114 before deriving any concentration-like quantity.

THE NITRATE-TO-TOTAL-NITROGEN FRACTION IN IOWA TILE-DRAINED BASINS IS UNQUANTIFIED HERE. SPARROW predicts TOTAL nitrogen; this project predicts NITRATE. Deriving a nitrate-relevant feature from SPARROW TN requires assuming that fraction is stable across basins. No verified source in this corpus quantifies it or tests its spatial stability. If the fraction varies systematically between basins, it introduces exactly the kind of between-site error the feature is meant to reduce.

WHETHER A PRE-ACCUMULATED TILE-DRAINAGE ATTRIBUTE EXISTS IN THE WIECZOREK NHDPlus 'SELECT ATTRIBUTES' SERIES IS UNRESOLVED. A keyword search reportedly returned 0 hits, but this was assessed as likely a query-syntax problem rather than proof of absence. If such a member exists in _tot form it would eliminate the basin-aggregation step and avoid streaming a 740 MB file for two columns. Worth ten minutes before committing to the large parse.

NO VERIFIED NEGATIVE RESULTS FROM THE PROCESS-GUIDED ML LITERATURE. The angle's rules call for actively hunting failures, and the unverified corpus does report several promising-looking ones — transfer harming a large minority of targets, graph components failing at headwaters with no upstream neighbors, pretraining on non-spanning simulations degrading below the process model, pretraining gains decaying toward zero as labels densify. These are exactly the findings most worth having and NONE of them is verified. Several bear directly on whether this project's regime (label-rich in time, site-poor, no guaranteed upstream neighbor) is one where the technique pays off at all.
